transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Yeah, so... what finally pushed me to come in is that I just keep getting up from my desk when I know I really should stay put. Like, during sprint planning at work. I'm a software developer, and we actually just changed how we do our sprints—we got a new scrum master and he is super rigid about how we point our tickets, it's honestly kind of exhausting. 

But anyway, during those meetings, or even on personal stuff like mortgage calls... we're trying to buy a house right now, and the interest rates are just ridiculous. Plus we saw this one house last week that smelled entirely like vanilla extract, I don't know what they were baking, but they were definitely trying to cover something up. 

But yeah, I'll be on those important calls, and I'll just suddenly decide I desperately need a glass of water right that second, or I'll just get up to check something random in the other room. I know I should just sit there and focus, but I keep wandering off.
Did you experience similar difficulties sitting still or staying seated when you were a child in school?

Yeah, actually, I do remember that. In elementary school, my teachers were constantly moving my desk around or having to remind me to just stay seated. I was always popping up out of my chair for some reason, or I'd just start talking and blurting things out before they even called on me. And I'd always rush through my worksheets, even when I totally understood the material and knew how to do it. 

Which is funny to think about, because I remember those worksheets were always printed on that old ditto machine paper with the purple ink? I swear I can still smell that ink if I think about it. It had such a specific, sweet smell. Kind of like those little scented erasers everyone used to collect back in the nineties. I had this huge plastic pencil box full of the strawberry ones, but the chocolate ones always smelled like weird chemicals to me. My best friend Jess had literally hundreds of them, we would trade them all the time. We actually just connected on LinkedIn the other day, which is wild because she's a project manager now at a big logistics firm, and she used to be the most disorganized person I knew when we were kids. We're supposed to get coffee next week if I can actually find a gap in my sprint schedule, though with this new scrum master, I doubt it. 

But um... wait, I'm sorry, what were we just talking about? Oh, right, school. Yeah, they definitely had to tell me to sit down and stop rushing a lot back then.

Like, my work tickets, the notes for our home repairs, our budget reminders... they're all just completely scattered. I've got stuff in Slack, a million sticky notes, emails I've starred, random lists on my phone... I swear I spend more time figuring out what I was supposed to do than actually doing it. 

And the sticky notes are the worst because I buy those super bright neon ones—I refuse to buy the pastel ones, they're just depressing, you know? I always get the bright pink or the electric green. But I feel like the brand I buy lately loses its stickiness so fast! I stuck one to my car dashboard yesterday with a list of things we needed to fix the guest bathroom sink, and I rolled the window down because it was randomly so warm out, which is just crazy weather for this time of year, and the note blew right out the window. So I got to the hardware store and just ended up staring at PVC pipes for twenty minutes trying to remember what I actually went there for. The guy working in plumbing didn't even ask if I needed help, he was just talking to his coworker about some football game the whole time... 

Wait, sorry. What were you asking? Oh, right, tracking details. Yeah, my system is basically nonexistent right now, everything is just everywhere.
